rationale: The moments benchmark is a compute-bound, FP-arithmetic-intensive Shootout C++ program with hot inner loops and essentially no source-level metadata (empty profile), so the table favors passes that transform arithmetic and basic-block structure cheaply while penalizing anything that perturbs the hot loop path. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights because numeric code is dense in arithmetic/logic operations that substitution obscures at near-zero runtime and correctness cost; SPLIT is similarly cheap structural diversity with low risk weights. FLA carries a high RuntimeCost weight (0.8) so the selector only flattens functions whose features justify it, since control-flow flattening badly disturbs tight numeric loops; BCF is moderated (0.6 runtime/size) to allow some bogus-flow padding on cold functions without bloating the small binary. IBR gets a moderately high RuntimeCost (0.7) and the highest CorrectnessRisk (0.4) because indirect branches cost real dispatch time on hot paths and can interact badly with floating-point control flow; ICALL and IGV are kept mid-range since moments has few indirect calls and modest global-variable usage, letting the feature-driven selector apply them only where function features (e.g., many globals or call targets) actually favor those dimensions.
